The per-frame drive that made SpinPropellers reachable for an AEROPLANE (its only caller was the wind-tunnel fans). One MonoBehaviour per file, named after it. cs: Assets/Scripts/Flight/PropellerSystem.cs (incremental edit -- the lazy transparent switch; see the propeller.js base claim above for the file's own port)
note: NO NEW COVERAGE CLAIMED (propeller.js has no headroom left -- see above). Recorded because the edit changes real behaviour: SpinPropellers wrote `c.a = want` unconditionally, and a URP Lit material in its default OPAQUE surface mode ignores _BaseColor's alpha outright, so the blades never faded behind the blur disc at all. src/propeller.js:1115-1121 switches the material to transparent LAZILY -- `if (!b.material.transparent && want < 0.999) { ...transparent = true; depthWrite = true; }` and `if (b.material.transparent) b.material.opacity = want` -- and both halves matter here: a blade switched to transparent on frame 1 would pay transparent sorting for every stationary propeller in the plane hall AND read as glass to Combat/PlaneDamage.PartsOf's canopy test (IsTransparent && Alpha < 0.95). Ported as IsFadeable/MakeFadeable (URP: _Surface=1, alpha blend, _ZWrite kept at 1 for the JS's explicit depthWrite, _SURFACE_TYPE_TRANSPARENT). Also documented (not changed) at the hint.Make branch: why the hinted-hub path's x-component is the NEGATIVE of the JS's and must stay that way.
